source: GROUND.md §6.6 (G5, raiding). Raid costs are Rust's well-known tables, which the owner allows: how many of each explosive break each grade of wall (timed charge 1/2/4/8 for wood, stone, metal, armoured; rockets 2/4/8/15; bag charges 3/10/23/46; tin grenades 13/46/112/223; explosive rounds 49/185/400/799) and each door (timed charge 1/1/2/2 for wooden, sheet metal, garage and armoured; rockets 1/2/3/4; bag charges 2/4/9/12; explosive rounds 19/63/150/200). The damage of one hit is set so those counts come out on our hit points (RustMVP's 10/200/500/1000/2000; doors 200/250/600/1000), so against wood (200, Rust's 250) and the armoured door (1000, Rust's 800) it differs from Rust's while the counts match. Damage is kept to the fraction, so a grenade's 8.99 against metal takes 112, not 100. Explosives hurt both sides of a wall alike (Rust); a grade may give [hard, soft] to tune that. The tin grenade's doors and the high-velocity rocket are ours, in proportion. Radii, falloff (full within 40% of the radius, nothing at it), the 30% splash on other pieces in sight and shielding by what is in the way are hollow-orbit's (js/game/construct.js explode, js/game/items.js EXPLOSIVE), as are the flesh damage of the charge, rocket and bag; the timed charge's 10 s fuse is RustMVP's and Rust's; the bag charge's 6-12 s fuse and one-in-five dud, and the grenade's, are Rust's in kind. Deployable damage, throws, bounces and the alerts' timing are ours. P2 (GROUND_SYSTEMS.md §6): which throwables are also put on a surface by hand is placement.json's list (the timed and bag charges), each by the charge rule there.

blasts.note: IW4 (KNOWN_PROBLEMS.md finding 26, the owner's direction): whoever it strikes dies, a bear (400) too: 600 to the person or animal struck, so even 80% protection leaves 120 of a player's 100; the rest in reach take its blast's 175 as before.
IW4 (IRON_WAKE.md §7, the owner's proposals): a small burst, the fuel thrown out; the fire it leaves does the work.

fires.note: IW4 (IRON_WAKE.md §7): the fires a blast leaves (a blast's "fire" names its kind). Burning fuel rests on what the blast hit when that faces up within 'steepest' degrees; on anything steeper (a wall, a hull's side, a trunk, a body) or in the air it runs and falls straight down to the first surface that does, at most 'runsDown' metres below (none: no fire). A fire on water or in the sea goes out at once; at most 'most' burn in a zone, the oldest going first; fires don't spread. A kind: its radius, the share of it it does all its damage within ('inner', as a blast's), how long it burns, how often it hurts ('every', seconds), and what it does a second at its middle, nothing at its edge: to people and animals ('flesh', less what people wear on the body), the burning it sets in people while they are in it ('burning', survival.json's vital: 2 a second until it runs out or they swim), to deployables that burn ('deployables'; deployables.json 'burns') and to the building through its rules' heat channel ('building'; building.json gives twig and wood 1, stone and up 0).

kinds.note: The incendiary rocket's: a 3.5 m pool of burning fuel for 18 s. A wooden wall (200) in it loses 108, two fires break it; a small box (150) struck takes the burst's 60 and the fire's 90.
